overall: The draft covers the rulings tables well: every 2026-09-23/24/25 ruling that moved a number or added text is present, all nineteen blue-sky R-rows are present, and the help's new options are all present except that level() is treated as pre-existing. The structural problem is duplication: about twenty-five changes are narrated in two, three or four sections (ccc centring in S1 and S4; the dose-cell drop in S1, S4 and S6; the refit removal in S2, S4 and S6; the elasticity removals in S1, S4, S5 and S6; SI-7 in S1, S4 and S5; the joint pre-trend caution, simultaneous bands, e(V) blocks, escomp, anticipation, untreatedZero, containment, oldsyntax, ties, bootalpha, permrawp, PS-46, the prefixes, DF-1 and latticeignoreweights each twice). Nearly every contradiction listed above is one change told twice with drifting numbers, dates or attributions (the elasticity gap, the few-treated permute caution, SEB-05, did_imputation, anticipation, escomp, impvalues reweighting, the ame remedy list). The fix is one home per change with a cross-reference, and a final pass that checks each item against the evening rulings of 2026-09-25 (m175 built, SEB-05 withdrawn), which two items still describe as pending. The omissions are mostly 'leave it' rulings on known failures (contreatpoly(2) and lattice() all-zero covariances, poisson untreatedZero, F012, CS-74) and the BS-38 help sentence, which the pare-down appears to have deleted after it was ruled. Bug fixes to remove or trim are listed with the ruled half to keep; DF-1 and the latticeignoreweights re-bin are borderline and can stay once each. The register is plain and dash-free; the residue is process talk about what is 'held for his confirmation' and about test-suite counts, plus a dozen unintroduced package and Stata names (jwdid, bayesboot, ritest, boottest, event_plot, Mata, set emptycells drop) and the never-glossed Stata return codes.
